rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR SUN CI PHYIN DU RGOL BA GA LA YOD, GANG GIS NA RANG GI PHYOGS GZHAG TU MED CING GZHAN GYI PHYOGS BZLOG PA DON DAM PAR 'DOD PA'I MTSAN NYID BYAS PA 'DI, SUN CI PHYIN DU RGOL BA PA'I YANG DAG PA'I MTSAN NYID DU 'GYUR BA,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir sun ci phyin du rgol ba ga la yod, gang gis na rang gi phyogs gzhag tu med cing gzhan gyi phyogs bzlog pa don dam par 'dod pa'i mtshan nyid byas pa 'di, sun ci phyin du rgol ba pa'i yang dag pa'i mtshan nyid du 'gyur ba
rows.english: How then could there ever be an opponent that we overcame? Suppose that there were no position of our own that we could ever put forward, but that at the same time we posited some definitive statement that could put a stop to the other side's position. This would in itself require a definitive opponent—one that existed really, in order for us to overcome.

rows.acip: STONG PA NYID BDEN PAS STONG PAR GSUNGS PA NI STONG NYID DAM CHOS NYID LA DNGOS PO STE BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA'I BLO CAN GYI BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA BZLOG PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR RGYAL BA'I YUM LAS GSUNGS PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: stong pa nyid bden pas stong par gsungs pa ni stong nyid dam chos nyid la dngos po ste bden par 'dzin pa'i blo can gyi bden par 'dzin pa bzlog par bya ba'i phyir rgyal ba'i yum las gsungs pa yin no
rows.english: These statements that emptiness itself is empty of any true existence were made in the Mother Sutras themselves, in order to block the tendency to hold things as being real, in the thoughts of those whose minds were already grasping to the idea that things could be real: who were holding that emptiness or ultimate reality itself was a real thing.

rows.english: The fact that all ten directions of east and the rest are empty of existing through any essential nature of their own is “great emptiness.” And it was taught in order to stop people from holding that the directions are vast in a way that exists through some nature of its own. An example of taking the directions in a mistaken way would be where the River school called the Detailers holds that a direction represents some perfectly unchanging substance. 6) Ultimate emptiness

rows.acip: 'DI NI TING 'DZIN RGYAL PO LAS, YOD MED DANG GTZANG MI GTZANG GI MTHA' GNYIS SPANGS NAS, DBUS LA'ANG GNAS PAR MI BYED DO, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR MTHA' SPANGS PA'I DBUS BDEN NAM SNYAM PA'I BDEN 'DZIN BZLOG PA'I PHYIR DU GSUNGS PA STE,
rows.wylie: 'di ni ting 'dzin rgyal po las, yod med dang gtsang mi gtsang gi mtha' gnyis spangs nas, dbus la'ang gnas par mi byed do, zhes gsungs pa ltar mtha' spangs pa'i dbus bden nam snyam pa'i bden 'dzin bzlog pa'i phyir du gsungs pa ste
rows.english: All this recalls for example the King of Concentration, where it says that we should give up pairs of extremes such as existing or not existing; or else being clean or not being clean; but that neither should we then stay somewhere in the middle between these extremes. This was spoken to help us stop our habit of wondering whether or not the view in the middle might exist in truth, once we have eliminated the two extremes in each case.

rows.acip: DE LTAR BSHAD PA LAS BZLOG PA NI GNAS MIN PA ZHES BYA STE, DPER NA DGE BA LAS RNAM SMIN YID DU MI 'ONG BA 'BYUNG BA DANG, MTHONG LAM THOB PAS LAS DBANG GIS SRID PA BRGYAD PA 'GRUB PA NI GNAS MA YIN ZHING GO SKABS MED PA LTA BU'O,,
rows.wylie: de ltar bshad pa las bzlog pa ni gnas min pa zhes bya ste, dper na dge ba las rnam smin yid du mi 'ong ba 'byung ba dang, mthong lam thob pas las dbang gis srid pa brgyad pa 'grub pa ni gnas ma yin zhing go skabs med pa lta bu'o
rows.english: Anything that could happen in the opposite way from what we have described here then would be called what is “not actual.” For example, it would not be actual (there would be no chance of it) if a virtuous action led to an unpleasant ripening; or if an individual had attained the path of seeing and then—due to the power of karma—were to experience an eighth rebirth afterwards.

rows.english: And then there are cases of the opposite of these two; meaning that the karmas are mixed. And then there are the great variety of different ripenings that are produced by this path.

rows.english: What is the Reason for this? It is all because Those who are Not well versed Still possess A state of mind Where they have Strong craving. And because of this, They undergo Periods when they Are born & destroyed. They are torn From what feels Attractive, and Meet with The undesirable; They achieve The future fate of Those who still have Terrible deeds. The world Has crowded to Worthy objects Of compassion. As such, you— The Conqueror— Have, out of This compassion, Turned your heart Away from peace, Without allowing Yourself to go Into nirvana.

rows.wylie: 'jig rten gyi skye bo de rnams thugs brtse ba chen po'i yul du rab tu dong ba ste song bas na, thugs rje chen pos bcom ldan 'das khyod kyi thugs zhi ba phyogs gcig pa la gzhol ba las bzlog pas khyod la zhi ba phyogs gcig pa'i mya ngan las 'das pa mi mnga' bar 'jig rten du bzhugs so
rows.english: The beings of this world have “crowded to”—have become—worthy objects of great compassion. As such, “you”—the Conqueror—have, out of this great compassion, turned away from allowing your heart to be lost to but a partial state of peace. That is, you remain here in the world, but without allowing yourself to go into a kind of nirvana which represents one side of the condition of peace. How the commentary was composed

rows.english: He held a high level of knowledge that was never stolen away; and he possessed compassion as well. He was known for sketching a cow that was about to give birth, and then milking real milk from it. With this, he was able to stop others from believing that things are real. This then is the one who completed this composition.

rows.english: We must then for the short term go for shelter to the Three Jewels, to keep ourselves from a birth in the lower realms. We must as well open up and admit the things we have done wrong before, and restrain ourselves in the future. To do so we must make strong and heartfelt use of the four forces that counteract the power of the wrong. We must too put all our effort into taking up even the smallest virtue, and giving up even the slightest harms we commit

rows.english: Every trace of vegetation— from the roots, to the stalks, to the branches, to the twigs, and out to the leaves, would be crushed to powder. And every livingcreature there, would be smashed to dust. And as the mountains fell in it would happen in a minute, and no one would be able to outrun them, or force them back, or buy them off. Nor but with the greatest difficulty could you use any kind of magic substance, or magic words, or any sort of elixir to stop them.

rows.english: And what are these four terrors? They are aging, and sickness, and death, and trouble. Great King, I say to you: aging is the fact that our vitality is inevitably obliterated; sickness is the fact that our health is inevitably obliterated; trouble is the fact that any good thing that ever comes to us is inevitably obliterated; and death is the fact that our very life is inevitably obliterated. All four of these come to us, and we cannot outrun them, Nor but with the greatest difficulty could you use any kind of magic substance, or magic words, or any sort of elixir to stop them.

rows.acip: DE YANG LTUNG BA PHYIR BCOS NI SDOM PA GONG 'OG SO SO NAS GSUNGS PA LTAR BYA LA SDIG PA, PHYIR BCOS PA NI STOBS BZHI'I SGO NAS BYA STE CHOS BZHI BSTAN PA'I MDO LAS BYAMS PA BYANG CHUB SEMS DPA' SEMS DPA' CHEN PO CHOS BZHI DANG LDAN NA SDIG PA BYAS SHING BSAGS PA YANG ZIL GYIS GNON PAR 'GYUR RO BZHI GANG ZHE NA 'DI LTA STE RNAM PAR SUN 'BYIN PA KUN TU SPYOD PA DANG GNYEN PO KUN TU SPYOD PA DANG NYES PA LAS BZLOG PA'I STOBS DANG RTEN GYI STOBS SO ZHES GSUNGS TE BYAS SHING BSAGS PA'I LAS NI MYONG NGES YIN PAS DE ZIL GYIS GNON NUS NA MA NGES PA LTA CI SMOS

rows.english: Instances in which you have committed some transgression of your vows, at whichever level of vows you may have, should be repaired according to the methods prescribed for those particular vows. For repairing the damage caused by other kinds of bad deeds you should utilize the four powers. As the Sutra on the Four Practices states, O Loving One, if a great bodhisattva keeps four practices, then he or she can never be overwhelmed by bad deeds that they have both committed and collected. And what are these four practices? They are the activity of destruction, and the activity of an antidote, and the power of restoring, and the power of the The expression "committed and collected" refers to actions whose karmic results are "certain to be experienced." If even these types of karmic results can be overcome by the four practices, then there is no need to mention those which are not certain to be experienced. An Original Source for the Principle that Old Karma Can be Removed The general principle that old karma can be removed from our mind streams is clearly stated in a number of important works by Lord Buddha himself. One of the most famous of these is a part from the famous Diamond-Cutter Sutra, which appears in the following selection in bold lettering. The commentary that follows the sutra is the only known native Tibetan explanation of the work, and was composed by Chone Drakpa Shedrup (1675-1748) of the incomparable Sera Mey Tibetan Monastery. Chone Lama skillfully weaves the root text into his explanation, and these words have also been printed in bold. He moreover quotes several other important original sources to demonstrate that old karma can be removed.

rows.english: A person who relies on the Wish in the form of a prayer can rip out, from its roots, the obstacle created by the deed they've committed. There are a number of references we could use to demonstrate this fact. The young man named "Child of the Friend" wanted to travel across the sea to another land; his mother, for sheer love of the boy, would kneel and grasp him by his two legs, and was thus able to stop him. There came a point though where he was seized by violent anger at her, and he hit her on the head with his leg. Then he went to sea, but his ship went down in a storm. There was a near-hell at the edge of the ocean, and here the karma seed from disrespecting his mother was awakened. He heard a voice from the sky that said "Kneel here, for the crown of knives is about to spin down upon your head." And he stood, making to himself a fervent prayer: May the karma of all those who have ever disrespected their mother in the past; or who are disrespecting their mother at this moment; or who may ever in the future disrespect their mother all ripen upon me alone, at this very moment. May no one else ever suffer the pain that I am about to undergo.

rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. They are not though saying that there are no outside physical objects at all. The Asian Classics Institute Reading Two: How Emptiness Allows Karma to Work, According to the Middle-Way School

rows.wylie: 'o na shAn+ti pas dgra nag 'grel par, smad mi bya zhes bya ba ni rtsod pas sun dbyung bar mi bya ste 'gro ba dag ni rang rang gi 'dun pa'i theg pa tsam las rim gyis 'jus shing byang chub par 'gyur gyi btsan thabs su 'dun pa bzlog pa ni sdang ba 'phel ba'i rgyu tsam yin pas bzhag ste, zhes grub mtha' 'dzin pa sun 'byin pa la smod par gsungs pa ji ltar yin snyam na, sngags sam mtshan nyid kyi theg pa la skyon bkal nas bka' ma yin no, ,zhes sun phyung ba na de dag gi grub mtha' 'dzin pa'i yang 'dun pa ldog pa la bshad pas skyon med do
rows.english: "Well then," you may ask.  "How does it fit in here when Shantipa, in his commentary to the Ebony Enemy, describes the act of disparaging here as overthrowing the belief of a particular school?  He says, When the wording of the vow here says that we should "never disparage their beliefs," what it means is that we should not seek to overthrow others" beliefs through argument.  The point is that beings reach enlightenment by being taken up gradually, without overextending themselves past the particular way which they find comfortable at any given time.  If instead we undertake some drastic step to try to change their minds, it only causes hard feelings--and so for the time being we should let it be." And yet there's no problem here.  What Shantipa is referring to here is where we say something negative about either the secret or open ways of Buddhism, overthrowing it in the sense of saying "This is not the Word of the Buddha," and thus changing the person's mind: causing them to give up their desire to learn a particular school of Buddhism.

rows.acip: BLA MA'I DRUNG DU GZHAN GYIS PHYAG BYA BA SOGS BZLOG PA,
rows.wylie: bla ma'i drung du gzhan gyis phyag bya ba sogs bzlog pa
rows.english: If in our Lama's presence another person attempts to prostrate to us or anything of that nature, then we must stop them from doing so. B. The Mother Vows, Part One Our final group of tantric vows is the Mother Vows.  In this and the final class, we present the entire text of an extremely rare and secret commentary on these vows by the famed Mongolian sage, Kalka Damtsik Dorje (1781-1855).  His work is entitled The Shining Glory of Great Bliss: A Presentation of the Eight Pledges Spoken in the Root Tantra of Highest Bliss (bDe-mchog rtza-rgyud las gsungs pa'i dam-tsig brgyad gyi rnam-bzhag bde-chen dpal-'gyur). As we will see, this text draws large sections verbatim from Je Tsongkapa's own Cow that Produces Every Wish: An Extensive Explanation of the Practice of Realization for the Secret Teaching of the Conqueror, the Glorious Sphere of Highest Bliss (Heruka), found at ACIP digital text S5320. ***

rows.english: You can also read the lines as saying that Crowface and the rest of the eight Guardians cause your respect and devotion to come to increase; and that these emotions are the cause of every spiritual attainment.  The point here is that, as we noted before, the cause of every spiritual attainment is to always (meaning continually) feel respect for one's Lama and for deep practitioners who follow this secret teaching.  And the Guardians of the Gates can help us stop any hindrances which might prevent this respect and faith from growing ever higher; as such, they are causes that help these emotions increase.

rows.acip: GRVA PA GZHAN GYI PHRAG DOG GIS DMAG DRANGS BYUNG BA SPRUL PA'I DMAG GIS PHYIR BZLOG PAS GUS SHING SLOB MAR GYUR, THANG LHA DANG SHAB KYI 'BA' RA NAG PO LA SOGS PA BAR CHAD BYED DU BYUNG BA'I LHA 'DRE RNAMS NYIN MO THOG DANG MTSAN MO TING NGE 'DZIN GYIS ZIL GYIS MNAN ZHING SROG SNGAGS BLANGS TE DAM TSIG LA BZHAG
rows.wylie: grva pa gzhan gyi phrag dog gis dmag drangs byung ba sprul pa'i dmag gis phyir bzlog pas gus shing slob mar gyur, thang lha dang shab kyi 'ba' ra nag po la sogs pa bar chad byed du byung ba'i lha 'dre rnams nyin mo thog dang mtshan mo ting nge 'dzin gyis zil gyis mnan zhing srog sngags blangs te dam tshig la bzhag
rows.english: At one point it happened that some other monks, out of envy towards Kyungpo Neljor, actually organized a group of armed men to do Him violence.  He routed the soldiers though by emanating an army of His own, which grained the monks' respect, and they became His disciples. In these days too a great many spirit beings of obstruction made their appearance—demons such as the Spirit of the Plains, and the Ebony Devil of Shab.  When they came in the daytime, Kyungpo Neljor blasted them with bolts of lightning; those who came at night He overwhelmed with the power of His meditation.  Then He used mantras to capture their life-force, and bound them to His service.

rows.acip: 'PHO BA NI, 'CHI LTAS BYUNG MA THAG NAS 'PHO BA BYED DU MI RUNG BAS 'CHI LTAS BYUNG NA 'CHI BA BLU BA'I THABS GANG ZAB LA 'BAD DGOS, 'CHI BLU BYAS KYANG MI BZLOG PA BYUNG NA, ZLA BA DRUG GI GONG ROL NAS 'PHO BA BYA CHOG ,

rows.english: Here are some notes on the practice of transferring your mind.  Transferring your mind this way is not something you should be doing right after you get a sign that you are going to die.  Therefore when such a sign occurs you should put all your effort into carrying out the deepest practice you can find for ransoming death.  If you do complete one of these practices and are still unable to reverse your impending death, then six months before it comes you are allowed to do the transfer.

rows.english: And then the Master decided to return to the city, for three reasons.  First of all, He wanted to put a stop to the lack of faith that people were feeling towards Him, by showing them the pureness of His actions.  He further wanted to accomplish the purpose for which the emanation of the Compassionate One had been invited, in order to help lower kinds of living beings in the future.  And then thirdly He had the idea that He could get the people of the country of Oddivisha to enter the diamond way.  He set off then for the city, bringing along with him a little boy and a little girl that He had emanated.

rows.english: When they state this way that--if you can't find an outer woman, then you can practice with an imaginary one--it's with reference to the fact that practice with an imaginary partner doesn't have the capacity to bring on in us the meditation of great bliss in the same way that practice with an actual partner does.  To say though that you do find an outer woman, and then leave off practicing with Her, and practice instead with an imaginary woman, is to interpret the lines in a completely opposite way than what we've seen above.

rows.acip: YAN LAG BCU GNYIS PO THAMS CAD KYANG SEMS GCIG LA BRTEN PAR GSUNGS PA LA BRTEN NAS, TZAM GYI SGRAS SEMS GTZO BOR GYUR PAR BSTAN TE, BSHAD PA SNGA MA DGAG PHYOGS DANG PHYI MA SGRUB PHYOGS NAS YIN NO, , DE'I PHYIR 'GRO BA RAB TU 'JUG PA LA SEMS NYID GTZO BO'I RGYU YIN GYI, SEMS LAS GZHAN PA NI GTZO BO'I RGYU MIN PAS, MDO LAS SEMS TZAM ZHIG GTZO BOR BZHAG GI GZUGS NI MA YIN NO, , GAL TE GZUGS YOD PAR 'DOD MOD KYI STE KYANG GZUGS DE LA NI SEMS BZHIN DU 'GRO BA'I BYED PA PO NYID NI YOD PA MA YIN NO, , DES NA SEMS LAS GZHAN PA'I BYED PA PO BZLOG PA STE BKAG GI, PHYI ROL GYI GZUGS NI BKAG PA MA YIN NO, ,
rows.wylie: yan lag bcu gnyis po thams cad kyang sems gcig la brten par gsungs pa la brten nas, tsam gyi sgras sems gtso bor gyur par bstan te, bshad pa snga ma dgag phyogs dang phyi ma sgrub phyogs nas yin no, , de'i phyir 'gro ba rab tu 'jug pa la sems nyid gtso bo'i rgyu yin gyi, sems las gzhan pa ni gtso bo'i rgyu min pas, mdo las sems tsam zhig gtso bor bzhag gi gzugs ni ma yin no, , gal te gzugs yod par 'dod mod kyi ste kyang gzugs de la ni sems bzhin du 'gro ba'i byed pa po nyid ni yod pa ma yin no, , des na sems las gzhan pa'i byed pa po bzlog pa ste bkag gi, phyi rol gyi gzugs ni bkag pa ma yin no,
rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. They are not though saying that there are no outside physical objects at all. 93 The Asian Classics Institute Course V: How Karma Works Reading Six: How Emptiness Allows Karma to Work, According to the Middle-Way School

rows.english: The question and answer that appear in the first two sentences serve to identify constructs as what are being referred to when we speak of "things that lack any definitive nature." The part that begins with "And why do we speak of them as such?" serves as an answer to the question of what reason there is for us to describe them as such. Then Lord Buddha answers by giving us two reasons: one from the negative point of view, where he says that these things do not exist by definition; and one from the positive point of view, where he says that they are established through names and terms. The way in which the sutra approaches the question from these two different aspects can be understood to apply to the latter two attributes as well.

rows.english: The question and answer that appear in the first two sentences serve to identify constructs as what are being referred to when we speak of "things that lack any definitive nature." The part that begins with "And why do we speak of them as such?" serves as an answer to the question of what reason there is for us to describe them as such. Then Lord Buddha answers by giving us two reasons: one from the negative point of view, where he says that these things do not exist by definition; and one from the positive point of view, where he says that they are established through names and terms. The way in which the sutra approaches the question from these two different aspects can be understood to apply to the latter two attributes as well.

rows.english: The question and answer that appear in the first two sentences serve to identify constructs as what are being referred to when we speak of "things that lack any definitive nature." The part that begins with "And why do we speak of them as such?" serves as an answer to the question of what reason there is for us to describe them as such. Then Lord Buddha answers by giving us two reasons: one from the negative point of view, where he says that these things do not exist by definition; and one from the positive point of view, where he says that they are established through names and terms. The way in which the sutra approaches the question from these two different aspects can be understood to apply to the latter two attributes as well.

rows.wylie: yan lag bcu gnyis po thams cad kyang sems gcig la brten par gsungs pa la, brten nas tsam gyi sgras sems gtso bor gyur par bstan te bshad pa snga ma, dgag phyogs dang phyi ma sgrub phyogs nas yin no de'i phyir 'gro ba rab tu 'jug pa, la sems nyid gtso bo'i rgyu yin gyi sems las gzhan pa ni gtso bo'i rgyu min pas mdo las sems tsam zhig gtso bor bzhag gi gzugs ni ma yin no gal te gzugs yod par 'dod mod kyi ste kyang gzugs de la ni sems bzhin du 'gro ba'i byed pa po nyid ni yod pa ma yin no des na sems las gzhan pa'i byed pa po bzlog pa ste bkag gi phyi rol gyi gzugs ni bkag pa ma yin no
rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. These references convey yet another meaning of the word "only" in the expression "mind-only." Here the point is that mind is the main thing. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. Therefore all these scriptural references are denying that the opposite of the mind, something other than the mind, could be the creator. They are not though saying that there are no outside physical objects at all. The Asian Classics Institute Reading Two: How Emptiness Allows Karma to Work, According to the Middle-Way School

rows.english: It is true that craving is this way, because those who have been brought down by the tendency to conceive of what's not happiness as being happiness dive as a result of this into "everything," which refers to unworthy things and goals. rows.english: There is not. In general, all motivation may be divided into two types: the motivation had during the causal stages of a deed and the one we give the name of "motivation at the time." The first of the two acts to set you off: this is where you say before any particular action, "I'm going to do this or that." The second's function is to make you continue on: this is where you say to yourself after you've already started, "Now I'll do this act."

rows.english: It is stated in scripture as well that each and every one of the twelve links in the chain of interdependence depends on a single thing: the mind. The former scriptural references are putting their point in a negative way, and the latter references are putting their point in a positive way. Thus we can see that it's the mind which is the one single principal cause that sets all life into motion. The principal cause is not something other than the mind. Therefore when the sutras speak of "mind only," they are making the point that mind is the main thing, and not matter. Although we do of course admit that physical matter exists, this matter is not the one prime creator of sentient beings in the way that mind is. rows.english: In the Greater Steps of the Path, the Sutra Requested by Ocean of Understanding is first quoted. Then Lord Tsongkapa goes on to describe the example of a family person with an especially beloved son who suddenly falls into a great pit of filth. Even practitioners of the Listener and Self-Made Buddha types possess a kind of compassion which is similar to the one that the boy's mother and different relations feel, where they wish to pull him out of the pit. Only a bodhisattva though, he says, possesses the kind of compassion which is like the concern felt by the boy's father.

rows.english: It should be noted that the above view is only that of the present school. According to the great vehicle, the freedom achieved by listeners and self-made victors is not a final sort of freedom. Moreover, the prick of His foot by the sandalwood thorn and the other events mentioned above were only a show that the Buddha put on for the sake of His disciples. Actually the Buddha is completely incapable of suffering, for He has liberated himself from every possible problem, ranging from those of a normal suffering life up to those of a lower nirvana. The sutra known as Developing the Three Bodies of a Buddha does though speak of the two form bodies of the Buddha as being nirvana with something remaining, and of the phenomena body as being a nirvana with nothing remaining.

rows.english: Let us first consider enemy destroyers of the Listener or Self-Made Buddha type. Aren't you saying then that, like the non-Buddhists, they fail to eliminate all the widespread mental afflictions that operate in all three realms? Because isn't it true that they have failed to achieve the path which is directly incompatible, in the way it holds its object, with the root of all these afflictions; that is, the tendency to conceive of things as existing through some nature of their own? And this is true, for they lack that comprehensive knowledge where they realize that things have no nature of their own.

rows.english: (12) The root downfall of causing a person to turn back from total enlightenment Committing this begins when you say the following to a person who has already developed the wish to achieve total enlightenment: You will never be able to carry out the six perfections, and actually reach Buddhahood. rows.wylie: gal te skyes bu chung 'bring gi lam gnyis skyes bu chen po'i lam gyi gol sa yin na, de'i gegs sam mi mthun phyogs yin pa'i phyir 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs kyang ma yin par 'gyur ro zhe na, skyon med de, lam de gnyis skyes bu chen po myur du 'tshang rgya ba'i lam gyi gol sa yin pas de 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs ma yin kyang , nyan rang rnams rim gyis rgyud smin te 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs su 'gyur ba la 'gal ba ci yang med pa'i phyir ro, , de yang rang nyid gcig pu zhi bde don gnyer gyi blo lta bu la gtso bor dgongs pa'o
rows.english: Someone might then make the following objection. Suppose those two paths for people of lesser and medium capacity really are grave points of error for people of greater capacity. In that case, they would have to be an obstacle toward, or even in contradiction with, the path of the greater way. And then they could never constitute a method for reaching enlightenment. But the objection is unfounded. Those two paths do constitute a grave error in the path for people of greater capacity; they prevent these people from reaching enlightenment quickly. From this point of view then, these two paths are not a method for reaching enlightenment, but it's no contradiction at all to say that they constitute a method for reaching enlightenment, in the sense that they act to gradually ripen the mental continua of listeners and "self-made" Buddhas. The point about being a grave error refers primarily to details such as the state of mind where one aspires to reach a state of blissful peace for oneself alone.

rows.english: Here is the second. I also rejoice in the fact that beings have collected together good deeds such as those which are consistent with reaching freedom: those deeds which act as a cause for the enlightenment of the listeners and self-made Buddhas. rows.english: Here is the first section. One might have the following thought: It's true that, in order to help put an end to the entire amount of suffering that exists in other people, we must achieve matchless enlightenment. And for this reason we must realize thusness. How could it be though that, in order to put an end only to that suffering which exists in ourselves, we would also have to realize thusness? Remember though that our Protector, Nagarjuna, has said the following: As long as a person possesses the habit Of grasping to the heaps as true, For just this long will they also grasp To the thought that these are "me." He is saying here that, as long as we still possess the habit of grasping to our heaps as true, then for just this long will we find ourselves unable to reverse our "view of destruction": our tendency to view these heaps as being "me" or "mine," in a way where they exist through some nature of their own. To do this though, one must finish off one's tendency to grasp to the heaps as existing in truth. As such, the Protector is here stating the position that realized beings of these two types as well have realized that the heaps have no true existence. rows.english: Here is the first. It is true though that one must definitely realize emptiness even to achieve the goal of becoming an enemy destroyer. This is because of the fact that scriptural authority, in the form of the body of sutras devoted to the perfection of wisdom, states that--without habituating oneself to this path, where you realize emptiness--one can never reach the three "states of enlightenment."

rows.wylie: gsum pa ni, des na sngar bshad pa de ltar stong pa nyid kyi phyogs la sun 'byin pa ni 'thad pa ma yin te 'og nas 'chad pa'i rigs pa rnams kyis kyang gnod pa'i phyir ro, , des na nyan rang gi byang chub thob par 'dod pas kyang the tshom mi za bar stong pa nyid ni bsgom par bya ste, bden 'dzin 'khor ba'i rtsa bar gyur pa'i nyon mongs can gyi ma rig pa yin la de'i zhen yul sun ma phyung bar thar pa thob pa mi srid pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Here is the third point, [which is advice to those who seek to attain liberation, that it is therefore very right that they should meditate upon emptiness]. As such--that is, as we have just explained--the case is that all these attempts to overthrow those who accept the idea of emptiness are completely incorrect. They will also be disproved by the various kinds of reasoning which we will present later on. And so it is that even those who wish no more than to achieve the "enlightenment" which is the goal of the Listener and "Self-Made Buddha" tracks must still, beyond a shadow of a doubt, meditate upon emptiness, for the following reason. The tendency to hold things as existing truly is that form of ignorance, involved with mental affliction, which is the root of the circle of suffering. And it is completely impossible to attain freedom unless one can overthrow the existence of the object which this ignorance thinks it sees.

rows.english: In the Greater Steps of the Path, the Sutra Requested by Ocean of Understanding is first quoted. Then Lord Tsongkapa goes on to describe the example of a family person with an especially beloved son who suddenly falls into a great pit of filth. Even practitioners of the Listener and Self-Made Buddha types possess a kind of compassion which is similar to the one that the boy's mother and different relations feel, where they wish to pull him out of the pit. Only a bodhisattva though, he says, possesses the kind of compassion which is like the concern felt by the boy's father.

rows.english: Let us first consider enemy destroyers of the Listener or Self-Made Buddha type. Aren't you saying then that, like the non-Buddhists, they fail to eliminate all the widespread mental afflictions that operate in all three realms? Because isn't it true that they have failed to achieve the path which is directly incompatible, in the way it holds its object, with the root of all these afflictions; that is, the tendency to conceive of things as existing through some nature of their own? And this is true, for they lack that comprehensive knowledge where they realize that things have no nature of their own.

rows.english: Here is the first section. One might have the following thought: It's true that, in order to help put an end to the entire amount of suffering that exists in other people, we must achieve matchless enlightenment. And for this reason we must realize thusness. How could it be though that, in order to put an end only to that suffering which exists in ourselves, we would also have to realize thusness? Remember though that our Protector, Nagarjuna, has said the following: As long as a person possesses the habit Of grasping to the heaps as true, For just this long will they also grasp To the thought that these are "me." He is saying here that, as long as we still possess the habit of grasping to our heaps as true, then for just this long will we find ourselves unable to reverse our "view of destruction": our tendency to view these heaps as being "me" or "mine," in a way where they exist through some nature of their own. To do this though, one must finish off one's tendency to grasp to the heaps as existing in truth. Now there is no one at all who would claim that enemy destroyers of the Listener or Self-Made Buddha types have not yet eliminated their "view of destruction" in its entirety. rows.wylie: dang po ni, nyan rang dgra bcom pa'i 'bras bu thob pa la yang stong nyid rtogs pa nges par dgos par thal, rgyu mtshan gang gi phyir na shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa'i mdo sde'i lung las stong nyid rtogs pa'i lam 'di ni goms pa med par byang chub gsum ga thob pa med par gsungs pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Here is the first. It is true though that one must definitely realize emptiness even to achieve the goal of becoming an enemy destroyer. rows.acip: GSUM PA NI, DES NA SNGAR BSHAD PA DE LTAR STONG PA NYID KYI PHYOGS LA SUN 'BYIN PA NI 'THAD PA MA YIN TE 'OG NAS 'CHAD PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KYANG GNOD PA'I PHYIR RO, , DES NA NYAN RANG GI BYANG CHUB THOB PAR 'DOD PAS KYANG THE TSOM MI ZA BAR STONG PA NYID NI BSGOM PAR BYA STE, BDEN 'DZIN 'KHOR BA'I RTZA BAR GYUR PA'I NYON MONGS CAN GYI MA RIG PA YIN LA DE'I ZHEN YUL SUN MA PHYUNG BAR THAR PA THOB PA MI SRID PA'I PHYIR RO,
rows.wylie: gsum pa ni, des na sngar bshad pa de ltar stong pa nyid kyi phyogs la sun 'byin pa ni 'thad pa ma yin te 'og nas 'chad pa'i rigs pa rnams kyis kyang gnod pa'i phyir ro, , des na nyan rang gi byang chub thob par 'dod pas kyang the tshom mi za bar stong pa nyid ni bsgom par bya ste, bden 'dzin 'khor ba'i rtsa bar gyur pa'i nyon mongs can gyi ma rig pa yin la de'i zhen yul sun ma phyung bar thar pa thob pa mi srid pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Here is the third point, [which is advice to those who seek to attain liberation, that it is therefore very right that they should meditate upon emptiness]. As such--that is, as we have just explained--the case is that all these attempts to overthrow those who accept the idea of emptiness are completely incorrect. They will also be disproved by the various kinds of reasoning which we will present later on. And so it is that even those who wish no more than to achieve the "enlightenment" which is the goal of the Listener and "Self-Made Buddha" tracks must still, beyond a shadow of a doubt, meditate upon emptiness, for the following reason. The tendency to hold things as existing truly is that form of ignorance, involved with mental affliction, which is the root of the circle of suffering. And it is completely impossible to attain freedom unless one can overthrow the existence of the object which this ignorance thinks it sees.

rows.english: This brings us to our second point from above, on the actual path itself.  Members of the Independent branch of the Middle Way would say that each overall path through each of the three tracks consists itself of five paths, starting with the path of accumulation.  Those of the Independent branch who lean towards the Sutrist system would say that listeners and self-made buddhas are equivalent in the sense that they are, primarily, working to eliminate obstacles to nirvana.  And they would say that there are no great degrees of higher or lower between these two tracks.

rows.english: What this is saying is that you could lump together all the good karma accumulated by all the listeners, and all the self-made buddhas—and all the good karma that belongs to the world, or has gone beyond the world—and multiply it all by ten, and you would just have enough karma to produce a single fine hair growing out of a single pore on the skin of a Buddha. rows.acip: [E8] DE YANG GZHI SHES DANG, LAM SHES KYI RNAM PA NYAN RANG DANG, BYANG SEMS DANG, SANGS RGYAS LA RIM BZHIN THUN MONG DU YOD PAS RNAM MKHYEN GYI RNAM PA STON PA NA DE DAG DANG THUN MONG PA'I RTOGS PA RNAMS KYI RNAM PA YANG GYI DGOS SO, ZHES SHES PAR BYA BA'I PHYIR DANG,
rows.wylie: [e8] de yang gzhi shes dang, lam shes kyi rnam pa nyan rang dang, byang sems dang, sangs rgyas la rim bzhin thun mong du yod pas rnam mkhyen gyi rnam pa ston pa na de dag dang thun mong pa'i rtogs pa rnams kyi rnam pa yang gyi dgos so, zhes shes par bya ba'i phyir dang
rows.english: The point we're supposed to gather here is— The forms of realization known as foundation knowledge and path knowledge are shared by the overall process, as we consider stages advancing through those of the listeners, and then the bodhisattvas, and finally the full Buddhas. rows.english: We begin with the offering.  Here in Tsongkapa's first verse, the Buddhas are said to be Victors because they have won the victory over the four demons. And we are speaking here of the path that they have all taken.

rows.english: According to our own position, listeners and self-made buddhas—when they are in deep meditation upon the unstained—are directly realizing the lack of any self-nature to the person.  As such, their state of mind cannot be established as being stained, in the sense of being involved with the negative emotions.  Nonetheless—as we have explained previously—there is for example a way of positing this state as being stained, insofar as it is possessed of the tendency to believe in the self-nature of things, as opposed to the person.

rows.wylie: thub pa'i sgra ni nyan rang dgra bcom la yang 'jug mod kyang, thub pa'i dbang po min pas sangs rgyas nyid la thub pa'i dbang po zhes bya ste, nyan rang dang byang sems rnams las kyang gong na med pa'i chos kyi dbang phyug dam pa brnyes pa dang, gang zag gsum po de sangs rgyas kyi bkas chos kyi srid la mnga' sgyur ba'i phyir ro
rows.english: Now admittedly the term “able one” can be used with reference to enemy destroyers of both the listener or the self-made buddha type; these practitioners though are not “Lords of the Able,” and so it is only an Enlightened Being to whom we can refer with this expression. This is because an Enlightened Being has attained an eminent lordship of the teachings which is higher than any of that reached by any listener or self-made buddha—or even by any normal bodhisattva. Moreover, practitioners of all three of these types are invested in their power over the kingdom of the teachings precisely by the command of the Enlightened Ones.

rows.english: One might ask just how it is that the Lords of the Able do this “producing” of the listeners and the self-made. When an Enlightened Being comes to a planet, they engage in teaching—unerringly—the profound instructions upon dependent events. Practitioners who are attracted to the paths of the listener and self-made buddha then listen to these teachings; and contemplate upon what they have heard; and meditate upon the conclusions reached in their contemplations.

rows.acip: DE LTAR NA GZHAN LAS MCHOD BRJOD KYI YUL DU GRAGS PA'I NYAN RANG GNYIS DANG, SANGS RGYAS DANG BYANG SEMS LA 'DIR DNGOS SU MCHOD BRJOD MA MDZAD PA NI, DE RNAMS KYI RTZA BA'I RGYU LA MCHOD BRJOD BYED PA YIN LA,

rows.english: As such, the reason that here in this context we make an offering of praise not to the two of the listeners & the self-made buddhas, nor to the Buddhas or bodhisattvas—at least, not directly—is that we are making this offering to their root cause.

rows.acip: DE LTA NA SANGS RGYAS KYIS NYE BAR BSTAN PA LAS, BYANG SEMS SKYE BA YIN KYANG, THUB DBANG SKYES ZHES PA'I SKABS SU, DE LA NYAN RANG LTAR BSHAD MI DGOS TE, DE GNYIS THUB DBANG LAS SKYES PAR STON PA NI, DE GNYIS KYI RTZA BA YANG MTHAR GTUGS NA, SNYING RJE LA THUG PAR BSTAN PA'I PHYIR YIN LA, BYANG SEMS KYI RTZA BA SNYING RJE LA THUG PA NI LOGS SU STON PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: de lta na sangs rgyas kyis nye bar bstan pa las, byang sems skye ba yin kyang, thub dbang skyes zhes pa'i skabs su, de la nyan rang ltar bshad mi dgos te, de gnyis thub dbang las skyes par ston pa ni, de gnyis kyi rtsa ba yang mthar gtugs na, snying rje la thug par bstan pa'i phyir yin la, byang sems kyi rtsa ba snying rje la thug pa ni logs su ston pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: It is then the case that bodhisattvas are born from receiving teachings from the Buddhas; nonetheless, we need not explain their birth in the way that we do with the listeners & self-made buddhas in the part about being “born from the Lords of the Able.” When we demonstrate how these two are born from the Lords of the Able, we are also saying that—ultimately—their very root traces back to compassion; and then we continue on to show separately how it is that the root of a bodhisattva traces back to this same compassion. The causes of a bodhisattva

rows.wylie: gsum pa ni, gal te nyan rang gnyis thub dbang las dang, thub dbang rnams byang sems las 'khrungs na, byang sems de dag gi rgyu gang yin zhe na
rows.english: This brings us to the third section from above: a description of the three principal causes of a bodhisattva. We may begin with the following question: “Given that both the listeners and the self-made buddhas are born from the Lords of the Able; and that these Lords themselves take their holy birth from the bodhisattvas; what then is it that serves as the cause of those bodhisattvas?” [I.1b]

rows.acip: CHOS GSUM BYANG SEMS KYI RGYUR STON PA 'DI NYAN RANG SANGS RGYAS LAS DANG, SANGS RGYAS BYANG SEMS LAS 'KHRUNGS NA, BYANG SEMS GANG LAS 'KHRUNGS ZHES DPYOD PA'I SKABS YIN PAS, BYANG SEMS KYI RNAM 'JOG GI RGYUR MI RUNG BAS SKYED BYED KYI RGYU'O,,
rows.wylie: chos gsum byang sems kyi rgyur ston pa 'di nyan rang sangs rgyas las dang, sangs rgyas byang sems las 'khrungs na, byang sems gang las 'khrungs zhes dpyod pa'i skabs yin pas, byang sems kyi rnam 'jog gi rgyur mi rung bas skyed byed kyi rgyu'o
rows.english: Now someone may come and raise the following objection: This section, where these three items are described as the causes of a bodhisattva, is a juncture where we are examining the question of what it is that gives bodhisattvas their holy birth—since we have just covered how listeners & self-made buddhas take their holy birth from Buddhas, and Buddhas themselves take theirs from bodhisattvas. As such, we must be talking about “causes” here in the sense of the causes which give birth to a bodhisattva, and not “causes” in the sense of the requirements for saying that someone is a bodhisattva.

rows.acip: GANG GI PHYIR SNYING BRTZE BA NI RGYAL BA'I LO TOG PHUN TSOGS 'DI'I THOG MAR SKYED PA LA GAL CHE BA SA BON DANG NI 'DRA LA, BAR DU GONG NAS GONG DU SPEL BA LA CHU DANG 'DRA ZHING, THA MAR GDUL BYAS YUN RING DU LONGS SPYOD PA'I GNAS LA, 'BRAS BU'I SMIN PA LTA BUR 'DOD PAR GYUR PA DE'I PHYIR, ZLA BA'I ZHABS BDAG GIS NYAN RANG DANG SANGS RGYAS DANG, BYANG SEMS DANG DE'I RGYU GZHAN GNYIS LAS KYANG THOG MAR RAM, BSTAN BCOS RTZOM BA'I THOG MAR SNYING RJE CHEN PO LA BSTOD PAR BGYI'O,,
rows.wylie: gang gi phyir snying brtse ba ni rgyal ba'i lo tog phun tshogs 'di'i thog mar skyed pa la gal che ba sa bon dang ni 'dra la, bar du gong nas gong du spel ba la chu dang 'dra zhing, tha mar gdul byas yun ring du longs spyod pa'i gnas la, 'bras bu'i smin pa lta bur 'dod par gyur pa de'i phyir, zla ba'i zhabs bdag gis nyan rang dang sangs rgyas dang, byang sems dang de'i rgyu gzhan gnyis las kyang thog mar ram, bstan bcos rtsom ba'i thog mar snying rje chen po la bstod par bgyi'o
rows.english: And so here at the beginning of the act of composing this classical commentary, I—that is, the great Chandrakirti—shall sing the praises of great compassion. (One could also read “beginning” here as referring to compassion itself, which precedes even the other two causes of a bodhisattva, and thus both full Buddhas and the listeners & self-made buddhas.) This I do for I believe that love is crucial, like the seed which—at the outset—produces those excellent crops of the Victors. And then in the interim love is like the water which makes these crops grow ever higher. And then at the end, finally, it is like the ripened fruit, which long afterwards is something that we disciples can enjoy.

rows.acip: BAR DU GAL CHE BA LA CHU DANG 'DRA TSUL NI, SNYING RJE'I SA BON GYIS BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS KYI MYU GU THOG MAR BSKYED DU ZIN KYANG, DUS PHYIS SNYING RJE'I CHUS YANG DANG YANG DU MA BCUS NA, 'BRAS BU SANGS RGYAS KYI RGYUR GYUR PA'I TSOGS GNYIS YANGS PA MA BSAGS PA 'DI, NGES PAR NYAN RANG GANG RUNG GI MYA NGAN LAS 'DAS PA MNGON DU BYED LA, SNYING RJE'I CHUS YANG YANG BCUS NA DE LTAR MI 'GYUR RO,,
rows.wylie: bar du gal che ba la chu dang 'dra tshul ni, snying rje'i sa bon gyis byang chub kyi sems kyi myu gu thog mar bskyed du zin kyang, dus phyis snying rje'i chus yang dang yang du ma bcus na, 'bras bu sangs rgyas kyi rgyur gyur pa'i tshogs gnyis yangs pa ma bsags pa 'di, nges par nyan rang gang rung gi mya ngan las 'das pa mngon du byed la, snying rje'i chus yang yang bcus na de ltar mi 'gyur ro
rows.english: Let's discuss next how it is that compassion is crucial during the middle period, in the same way that water is. It may well be the case that the seed of compassion has already, during the initial period, produced the fresh sprout of the Wish for enlightenment. If though during the time which follows we fail to apply the water of compassion to this sprout over & over, then we fail to accumulate any massive form of the two collections which serve as the cause of an Enlightened Being. This situation will then lead us, with certainty, to actualize only nirvana—either that of a listener, or of a self-made buddha. This is not the case when we do apply the water of compassion continuously.

rows.acip: THA MAR GAL CHE BA LA SMIN PA DANG 'DRA TSUL NI, ,RGYAL BA'I GO 'PHANG THOB TU ZIN KYANG SNYING RJE'I SMIN PA DANG BRAL NA, 'KHOR BA JI SRID KYI BAR DU SEMS CAN RNAMS KYIS NYE BAR LONGS SPYOD PA'I RGYUR MI 'GYUR ZHING, NYAN RANG DANG BYANG SEMS 'PHAGS PA'I TSOGS GCIG NAS GCIG TU BRGYUD PA BAR MA CHAD PA 'PHEL BAR YANG MI 'GYUR LA, 'BRAS BU'I SAR SNYING RJE CHEN PO RGYUN LDAN DU 'JUG NA DE LAS BZLOG STE 'BYUNG BA'O,,
rows.wylie: tha mar gal che ba la smin pa dang 'dra tshul ni, ,rgyal ba'i go 'phang thob tu zin kyang snying rje'i smin pa dang bral na, 'khor ba ji srid kyi bar du sems can rnams kyis nye bar longs spyod pa'i rgyur mi 'gyur zhing, nyan rang dang byang sems 'phags pa'i tshogs gcig nas gcig tu brgyud pa bar ma chad pa 'phel bar yang mi 'gyur la, 'bras bu'i sar snying rje chen po rgyun ldan du 'jug na de las bzlog ste 'byung ba'o
rows.english: Let's look finally at how it is that compassion is crucial at the end, like the ripened fruit. One may have already attained the state of a victorious Buddha; but if they were to lack the ripened fruit of compassion, then there would be nothing there for living beings to enjoy for all the time up to the last day of the cycle of pain. In this case, the continued accumulation of the causes for enlightenment by listeners & self-made buddhas, and realized bodhisattvas, could never proceed one to the other, growing in an uninterrupted stream. If though at the level of the final result one goes on with a continuous stream of great compassion in their heart, then the opposite occurs.

rows.acip: 'DI'I SNYING RJE GSUM NI DMIGS PA GSUM PO GANG LA DMIGS KYANG, SEMS CAN THAMS CAD SDUG BSNGAL MTHA' DAG LAS BSKYAB PAR 'DOD PA'I RNAM PA CAN YIN PAS, NYAN RANG GI SNYING RJE DANG KHYAD PAR SHIN TU CHE'O,,

rows.acip: GNYIS PA NI, GZHAN YANG SA DANG PO LA GNAS PA 'DI NI SO SKYE DANG NYAN RANG GI SA THAMS CAD LAS 'DAS PA'I PHYIR DANG, SANGS RGYAS KYI SA'I RJES SU 'GRO BAR NGES PA'I LAM RGYUD LA SKYES PA'I PHYIR DE BZHIN GSHEGS PA RNAMS KYI RIGS SU'ANG SKYES PA STE, LAM GZHAN DU MI 'GRO BAR RANG GI LAM DU RIGS NGES PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: gnyis pa ni, gzhan yang sa dang po la gnas pa 'di ni so skye dang nyan rang gi sa thams cad las 'das pa'i phyir dang, sangs rgyas kyi sa'i rjes su 'gro bar nges pa'i lam rgyud la skyes pa'i phyir de bzhin gshegs pa rnams kyi rigs su'ang skyes pa ste, lam gzhan du mi 'gro bar rang gi lam du rigs nges pa yin no
rows.english: This brings us to our second point from above: the high quality with the four characteristics which begin with taking birth into a royal family. We can moreover add that this person who is at the first bodhisattva level has taken birth into the family of Those Gone Thus—because they have gone far beyond the levels of common beings, and both the listeners & self made buddhas; and moreover because they have now given rise, within their hearts, to a path which is definite to lead them to the level of a Buddha. That is, they are confirmed within the family of their own path, and will never go off to some different path.

rows.acip: GNYIS PA LA GSUM, SA 'DIR NYAN RANG RNAMS RIGS KYI SGO NAS ZIL GYIS GNON PA DANG, SA BDUN PAR NYAN RANG GNYIS BLO'I SGO NAS ZIL GYIS GNON PA DANG, DE LTAR GSUNGS PAS GRUB PA'I DON BSHAD PA'O,,

rows.english: With this we have reached the second of our more general sections above—the high quality where our being outshines those of others. rows.acip: 'GREL BSHAD LAS SA BDUN PAR KHO BO LAM LA 'JUG PAR BYA'O SNYAM PA'I RNAM RTOG YOD PAS RTZOL BA DANG BCAS LA, MDO LA SOGS PA'I CHOS KYI MTSAN MA MNGON DU MI BYED PAS, MTSAN MA MED PA'I LAM THOB CING, DRUG PA MAN CHAD DANG NYAN RANG RNAMS LA MTSAN MED DE MED PAS, BLOS ZIL GYIS GNON PAR GSUNGS KYANG,
rows.wylie: 'grel bshad las sa bdun par kho bo lam la 'jug par bya'o snyam pa'i rnam rtog yod pas rtsol ba dang bcas la, mdo la sogs pa'i chos kyi mtshan ma mngon du mi byed pas, mtshan ma med pa'i lam thob cing, drug pa man chad dang nyan rang rnams la mtshan med de med pas, blos zil gyis gnon par gsungs kyang
rows.english: It is true that The Explanation speaks of how—at the seventh level—we still engage in discursive thought: we still say to ourselves, “I will practice the path”; and thus still exhibit conscious will. But we do not at this point still bring up mental forms of the physical manifestations of the teachings—the books of the sutras, or anything such; and so we can say that we have reached a “path free of the signs of things.” At the sixth and lower levels, continues this text, and with listeners & self-made buddhas, there is no “freedom from signs” of this kind.

rows.english: And yet there is no such concern, that the order of our presentation might be mixed up. The treatment in the present work of the first level and so on is based upon the Sutra on the Ten Levels; and in that scripture, the subject is covered by making a very definite distinction between the way that someone at the first level outshines the listeners & self-made buddhas by virtue of the deceptive form of the Wish for enlightenment which they possess, and the way that they do so by virtue of the ultimate form of this Wish that they have reached.

rows.english: And then, the sutra is saying, these listeners & self-made buddhas would end up being the same as those of other traditions—those of the lower systems, who have failed to eliminate everything connected to negative emotions, and the seeds for these, relating to any of the three realms. What this is saying is that—if we fail to perceive emptiness perfectly, and get used to what we perceived—then we could never be able to finish off the seeds for negative emotions; and then our efforts would end up being like those who follow the path of the world, trying to go from one discursive state of meditation to another, from rough to fine.

rows.english: These citations then are clearly indicating that, so long as one still lacks the view of suchness, they cannot be liberated from the cycle of pain; and in order to achieve such a liberation, one must possess this view. rows.acip: DE'I RKANG PA DANG PO GNYIS KYIS NI PHUNG PO LA BDEN PAR 'DZIN PA JI SRID YOD PA DE SRID DU, DE LAS NGAR 'DZIN PA'I 'JIG LTA 'BYUNG BAR BSTAN PAS, 'JIG LTA MA LUS PAR ZAD PA LA PHUNG PO BDEN 'DZIN ZAD DGOS PAR BSTAN TE, DE'I TSE NYAN RANG DGRA BCOM PAS KYANG PHUNG PO BDEN 'DZIN ZAD PAR SPANGS PAR SHES SO,,
rows.wylie: de'i rkang pa dang po gnyis kyis ni phung po la bden par 'dzin pa ji srid yod pa de srid du, de las ngar 'dzin pa'i 'jig lta 'byung bar bstan pas, 'jig lta ma lus par zad pa la phung po bden 'dzin zad dgos par bstan te, de'i tshe nyan rang dgra bcom pas kyang phung po bden 'dzin zad par spangs par shes so
rows.english: The very first part here, from “As long as one holds…” up to “…to a 'me',” is meant to indicate that—as long as one holds that the parts of a person are real—then one will be subject to the view of destruction that holds to a “me.” And what this implies is that—if one wishes to finish off every form of the view of destruction—then one must finish off the tendency to hold that the parts of the person are real. And we thus come to understand that at this point enemy destroyers who are listeners or self-made buddhas also eliminate the tendency to hold that the parts of the person are real.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR SLOB DPON 'DI'I LUGS KYIS NYAN RANG GIS GANG ZAG GI BDAG MED RTOGS TSUL, GRUB MTHA' SMRA BA GZHAN DANG 'DRA BA BZUNG NAS, CHOS KYI BDAG MED RTOGS PA YOD MED LA MI MTHUN PAR SMRA BAS NI, 'DI'I LUGS LEGS PAR MA RTOGS PA YIN TE,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir slob dpon 'di'i lugs kyis nyan rang gis gang zag gi bdag med rtogs tshul, grub mtha' smra ba gzhan dang 'dra ba bzung nas, chos kyi bdag med rtogs pa yod med la mi mthun par smra bas ni, 'di'i lugs legs par ma rtogs pa yin te

rows.acip: DES NA NYAN RANG LA CHOS KYI BDAG MED RTOGS PA YOD PAR BSHAD PA'I GZHUNG 'DZUGS PAR SGOM ZHING, NYON MONGS KYI RNAM GZHAG LA THUN MONG MA YIN PA'I 'JOG TSUL YOD DAM MED SNYAM PA TZAM YANG MI SKYE BA'I 'DI'I RJES 'BRANG RNAMS NI, LUGS 'DI LA DAD PA TZAM DU ZAD DO, ,'DIS MTSON NAS GZHAN YANG MANG DU SNANG BA RNAMS LEGS PAR RTZAD GCAD PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: des na nyan rang la chos kyi bdag med rtogs pa yod par bshad pa'i gzhung 'dzugs par sgom zhing, nyon mongs kyi rnam gzhag la thun mong ma yin pa'i 'jog tshul yod dam med snyam pa tsam yang mi skye ba'i 'di'i rjes 'brang rnams ni, lugs 'di la dad pa tsam du zad do, ,'dis mtshon nas gzhan yang mang du snang ba rnams legs par rtsad gcad par bya'o
rows.english: So what we have here is a person who has failed to sit down and put in front of their mind the great classics which explain how listeners & self-made buddhas do possess the perception that there is no self-nature to things; and to whom it has never even occurred to examine whether or not there is a unique way of setting forth how the negative emotions work. And then we have all of those who have followed this person, and who possess no more than a blind faith in our school. And all these people are only one example that we have dealt with here; there appear to be many others like them, and you should learn to scrutinize their views carefully.

rows.acip: THEG CHEN LAS NI, BYANG SEMS KYI SA RNAMS DANG, SBYIN PA LA SOGS PA'I PHAR PHYIN GYI SPYOD PA DANG, SMON LAM DANG BSNGO BA RLABS PO CHE RNAMS DANG, SNYING RJE CHEN PO SOGS DANG, TSOGS GNYIS RLABS PO CHE DANG, BYANG SEMS KYI MTHU RMAD DU BYUNG BA SO SKYE DANG, NYAN RANG GIS BSAM GYIS MI KHYAB PA'I CHOS NYID KYANG STON PA'I PHYIR TE,
rows.wylie: theg chen las ni, byang sems kyi sa rnams dang, sbyin pa la sogs pa'i phar phyin gyi spyod pa dang, smon lam dang bsngo ba rlabs po che rnams dang, snying rje chen po sogs dang, tshogs gnyis rlabs po che dang, byang sems kyi mthu rmad du byung ba so skye dang, nyan rang gis bsam gyis mi khyab pa'i chos nyid kyang ston pa'i phyir te
rows.english: And that's because the following subjects are also presented there: the levels of the bodhisattva; the activities of giving and the other perfections; vast and effective forms of prayer & dedication; great compassion and the like; powerful ways of completing the two collections; and the extraordinary might of the bodhisattva, the very nature of things, inconceivable to beings who have yet to see emptiness, and to the listeners & self-made buddhas.

rows.acip: DE NI THEG CHEN PA LA SHES BYA THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR RTOGS PA YOD LA, NYAN RANG LA DE MED PAR SHES BYA PHYOGS GCIG PA 'GA' RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA MED PAR RTOGS PA YOD CES PA NI, GTAN MIN TE
rows.wylie: de ni theg chen pa la shes bya thams cad rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par rtogs pa yod la, nyan rang la de med par shes bya phyogs gcig pa 'ga' rang bzhin gyis grub pa med par rtogs pa yod ces pa ni, gtan min te
rows.english: It is not at all the case, as some have put it, that this presentation is meant to convey that those of the greater way possess a realization that no existing object exists through any nature of its own; whereas those of the ways of the listener and the self-made buddha lack this same realization—since they realize only that some portion of all the things there are exist through no nature of their own.

rows.english: The reason this has come to be is that the listeners & self-made buddhas are making efforts towards nothing more than eliminating their negative emotions—and that may be done by perceiving the meaning of suchness in no more than but this abbreviated manner. Those of the greater way, on the other hand, are striving to rid themselves of the obstacles to knowledge; as such, they must develop wisdom towards suchness which grows in an exponential way: they must make their minds wide open. rows.acip: RTEN NI 'DIR DMIGS PA DANG, BRTEN PA NI DMIGS BYED YIN LA, DMIGS BYED LA NYAN RANG GI THEG PA GNYIS KYANG YOD CING, CHOS NYID LA DMIGS PA LA DE BLO NGOR 'GRUB DGOS LA, BDEN GRUB BLO NGOR MA BCAD PAR, BDEN STONG BLO NGOR MI 'GRUB CING, DE MA GRUB NA CHOS NYID BLO NGOR MI 'GRUB BO,,
rows.wylie: rten ni 'dir dmigs pa dang, brten pa ni dmigs byed yin la, dmigs byed la nyan rang gi theg pa gnyis kyang yod cing, chos nyid la dmigs pa la de blo ngor 'grub dgos la, bden grub blo ngor ma bcad par, bden stong blo ngor mi 'grub cing, de ma grub na chos nyid blo ngor mi 'grub bo
rows.english: The thing being relied upon here is the object of the perception; while what relies upon it is the state of mind doing the perceiving—and the mind doing the perceiving can also include the minds of those who belong to the two ways of the listener or the self-made buddha. And to say that one is perceiving the way things are, this way must have presented itself to the mind. Yet if one has yet to exclude the idea that things exist in truth from presenting itself to the mind, the idea that things are void of existing in truth cannot present itself—and so long as it does not, then the way things really are cannot.

rows.acip: DE LTAR GNYIS 'ONG BA NI MNGON RTOGS RGYAN DU NYAN RANG GI LAM SHES PA'I LAM SHES STON PA NI, NYAN RANG GI RIGS CAN RNAMS RJES SU 'DZIN PA'I PHYIR DU YIN PAS, RJES SU GZUNG RGYU'I THEG DMAN LA YANG ZAB MO'I SNOD DU GYUR MA GYUR GNYIS YOD CING, DE GNYIS LA'ANG PHYI MA CHE MANG BAS PHAL CHER DE'I LAM MANG DU GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: de ltar gnyis 'ong ba ni mngon rtogs rgyan du nyan rang gi lam shes pa'i lam shes ston pa ni, nyan rang gi rigs can rnams rjes su 'dzin pa'i phyir du yin pas, rjes su gzung rgyu'i theg dman la yang zab mo'i snod du gyur ma gyur gnyis yod cing, de gnyis la'ang phyi ma che mang bas phal cher de'i lam mang du gsungs so
rows.english: The fact that we see these two types relates to the fact that, in the Jewel of Realizations, the presentation of the knowledge of the path—where the listeners & self-made buddhas each know their own path—is something made in order to attract persons who fall into either the listener type or the self-made buddha type. As such, we can say that—among those of the lower way that the presentation is trying to attract—there are two types: those who are worthy vessels for the profound, and those who are not. And among these two types, the latter is by far more numerous; thus it is that for the most part, the path meant for them is spoken of more frequently.

rows.acip: GZUGS BRNYAN SOGS BRDZUN YANG SNANG BA NI BRDZUN PAR SNANG BA YIN LA, DE NI BYAD BZHIN DU SNANG BA DANG DES STONG PA GNYIS TSOGS PA'I BRDZUN PA YIN PAS, DE'I BDEN STONG NI BYAD BZHIN DU BDEN PAS STONG PA YIN GYI, GZUGS BRNYAN RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I BDEN STONG GI DON MED DO,,
rows.wylie: gzugs brnyan sogs brdzun yang snang ba ni brdzun par snang ba yin la, de ni byad bzhin du snang ba dang des stong pa gnyis tshogs pa'i brdzun pa yin pas, de'i bden stong ni byad bzhin du bden pas stong pa yin gyi, gzugs brnyan rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa'i bden stong gi don med do
rows.english: Reflections & the like can lie to us; but still they do make their appearance, in a lying way. This is a kind of lie where there is a combination of two things: something appearing to be the object which was placed in front of the mirror; and this something's being void of actually existing as that object. As such, when we speak of “voidness of reality” here what we are talking about is the fact that the reflection is void of any existing, in reality, as the object reflected. We are not referring here to a voidness of reality in the sense of the reflection being empty of any true existence, in the form of existing by definition.

rows.english: Let's consider objects such as visible or audible form, as these are established to be part of deceptive reality. Their nature is further one of a false construct, and not of truth, in the high perceptions of those listeners, self-made buddhas, and bodhisattvas who have rid themselves of misunderstanding which is involved with negative emotions; as well as in the perceptions of those who have seen that all factors are similar to a reflection in a mirror, or the like. To people such as these, these things have a nature of being a false construct, but not of being true—for these individuals are free of any mistaken fantasy that the things could be real.

rows.english: Thus it is too that the autcommentary says, We can use a reflection in the mirror to describe cause & effect which have no nature of their own. rows.acip: 'O NA DANG POR THEG CHEN DU ZHUGS PA'I DE KHO NA NYID KYI LTA BA LEGS PAR GTAN LA PHEBS PA ZHIG DANG, NYAN RANG DU LHUNG PA GNYIS GZHI MTHUN SRID PA NI DBU MA PA GNYIS KAS KYANG 'DOD DGOS LA, DE LTA NA DE 'DRA BA DES CHOS KYI BDAG MED BSGOMS PAS MNGON SUM DU 'GYUR BA DANG, DE LTAR MTHONG ZIN GOMS BAR BYED PA CIG KYANG 'DOD DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: 'o na dang por theg chen du zhugs pa'i de kho na nyid kyi lta ba legs par gtan la phebs pa zhig dang, nyan rang du lhung pa gnyis gzhi mthun srid pa ni dbu ma pa gnyis kas kyang 'dod dgos la, de lta na de 'dra ba des chos kyi bdag med bsgoms pas mngon sum du 'gyur ba dang, de ltar mthong zin goms bar byed pa cig kyang 'dod dgos so
rows.english: But first of all here we can say that we need to describe, accurately, how both of the groups within the school of the Middle Way would have to agree to the concept of one person who had just entered the greater way—and succeeded in establishing, accurately, the view of suchness—who at the same time could conceivably drop into the ways of the listeners, or the self-made buddhas. And they would have to agree that, in such a circumstance, the person who had done so could have a direct experience—since they had been meditating on the lack of a self-nature to things; and they could as well undertake to accustom themselves to what they had finished seeing.

rows.acip: 'DI LA GSAL BAR BSHAD PA MI SNANG YANG, RANG RGYUD PA DE DAG GIS NYAN RANG LAM DE LTAR SGOM PA LA, CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN MNGON GYUR RE ZHIG SPANGS PA 'ONG YANG, TSOGS MTHA' YAS PA BSAGS PA'I GROGS MED PAR CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS PO GANG GI YANG SA BON SPANGS PA MI 'ONG ZHES BZHED DGOS PAS, SHES SGRIB MNGON GYUR BA RE ZHIG LA SPANGS PA NYAN RANG LA SRID KYANG, SA BON SPANGS PA MI SRID PAR SMRA DGOS SO,,
rows.wylie: 'di la gsal bar bshad pa mi snang yang, rang rgyud pa de dag gis nyan rang lam de ltar sgom pa la, chos kyi bdag 'dzin mngon gyur re zhig spangs pa 'ong yang, tshogs mtha' yas pa bsags pa'i grogs med par chos kyi bdag 'dzin gnyis po gang gi yang sa bon spangs pa mi 'ong zhes bzhed dgos pas, shes sgrib mngon gyur ba re zhig la spangs pa nyan rang la srid kyang, sa bon spangs pa mi srid par smra dgos so
rows.english: I haven't observed a clear explanation of this point; but we can say that those who belong to the Independent group would have to agree that—if a person were to meditate in this way upon the paths of the listener or self-made buddha—then they would come to eliminate, for the time being, the manifest form of the tendency to hold to a self-nature to things. But they would also have to say that—without the additional assistance provided by accumulating unlimited masses of good karma—it is an impossibility that they could ever eliminate the seeds of either one of the two forms of the tendency to grasp to a self-nature of things. As such, one would have to declare that—even though it was possible for listeners and self-made buddhas to eliminate manifest forms of obstacles to omniscience for the time being—it would be impossible for them to have eliminated the seeds themselves.

rows.wylie: nyan rang rnams yang srid len pa med par mya ngan las 'da' la, byang sems ni de 'dra ba'i bdag med pa mthong du zin kyang, snying rje'i gzhan gyi dbang gis byang chub kyi bar du srid pa'i rgyun gyi skye ba 'dzin par byed do
rows.english: Bodhisattvas have long since seen that kind of lack of a self-nature which the listeners and self-made buddhas use to reach the nirvana where they no longer have to take a rebirth. But since they live at the mercy of thoughts of compassion, these bodhisattvas will still work to take a birth in the flow of lifetimes, until such time as they reach enlightenment.

rows.wylie: dgos pa ci'i phyir de gnyis bstan zhe na, gang zag gi bdag med ni nyan rang gi 'gro ba rnams 'khor ba las rnam par grol bar bya ba'i phyir bstan la, byang sems kyi 'gro ba rnams thams cad mkhyen pa thob pas rnam par grol bar bya ba'i phyir bdag med gnyis ka bstan no
rows.english: “What is the purpose,” one may ask, “of presenting these two types?” The lack of a self-nature to the person was taught in order to free beings who were listeners and self-made buddhas from the cycle of suffering. And both kinds of the lack of a self-nature were taught in order to free those beings who are bodhisattvas—which is what happens when they attain the state of omniscience.

rows.wylie: sngar bshad pa ltar nyan rang la yang rten 'brel rkyen nyid 'di pa tsam gyi de kho na nyid mthong ba yod mod kyang, de dag la sngar bshad pa ltar gyi chos kyi bdag med pa rnam grangs dang, dus kyi sgo nas yongs su rdzogs par sgom pa med pa ste, 'on kyang khams gsum gyi nyon mongs kyi sa bon spong ba'i thabs tsam zhig ni yod do
rows.english: As we explained earlier on, it is possible for listeners and self-made buddhas also to see suchness relating to this fact of causality: of dependence. But as we also explained earlier, these groups are incapable of meditating upon the lack of a self-nature to things in the entirety of the different expressions it takes, and relative to different times. We can say though that these practitioners do have in their possession just that method which allows them to eliminate the seeds for negative emotions relating to all three realms of the universe.

rows.wylie: yang na dmyal ba tsha grang sogs sdug bsngal che rim nas brtsams te sdug bsngal rgyu bcas, dang nyan rang sa bcu'i byang sems rnams kyi shes sgrib phra mo tshun chad sogs snod bcud thams cad kyi nyes skyon rnams blang
rows.english: Alternately you can begin with the greatest forms of suffering; for example, with the heat or cold in the hells, and take then upon yourself both the pain and its causes. Work all the way up to the most subtle obstacles to omniscience contained in the minds of listeners, self-made buddhas, and bodhisattvas at the tenth level; take upon yourself all the problems that exist in both the world around you, and in all those who live together with you here. rows.acip: PHAR GTONG BA'I TSE SKYABS 'GRO DANG LAS 'BRAS KYI DGE RTZA DANG ZAG MED KYI BDE BA RANG LA, MED KYANG YOD PAR MOS TE NGAN SONG GSUM LA BTANG BAS BDE 'GRO THOB LAM BSLAB PA GSUM GYI DGE RTZA MNGON MTHO'I GNAS LA BTANG BAS THAR PA THOB BYANG CHUB KYI SEMS DANG RGYAL SRAS KYI SPYOD PA'I DGE RTZA RNAMS NYAN RANG SOGS LA BTANG BAS SANGS RGYAS THOB PAR BSAM
rows.wylie: phar gtong ba'i tshe skyabs 'gro dang las 'bras kyi dge rtsa dang zag med kyi bde ba rang la, med kyang yod par mos te ngan song gsum la btang bas bde 'gro thob lam bslab pa gsum gyi dge rtsa mngon mtho'i gnas la btang bas thar pa thob byang chub kyi sems dang rgyal sras kyi spyod pa'i dge rtsa rnams nyan rang sogs la btang bas sangs rgyas thob par bsam
rows.english: When you do the practice of giving as you breathe out, think of the quantity of virtue you have in you from your acts of taking refuge, and observing the laws of karma and its consequences. Also imagine that you have some immaculate happiness to give, even though at this point we have yet to gain any. Do the act of giving all these, focusing on the those in the lower realms. See them reaching the higher realms as a result. Next take the quantity of virtue that you possess from following the path of the three trainings. Give it out to those in the higher realms, and imagine that Take finally the quantity of virtue you have from learning the Wish for enlightenment, and from following the way of life of the noble sons and daughters of the Buddhas. Imagine that you have given this virtue away to people like the listeners and the self-made buddhas. Imagine finally that this helps them reach Buddhahood itself.

rows.wylie: skyon med de, lam de gnyis skyes bu chen po myur du 'tshang rgya ba'i lam gyi gol sa yin pas de 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs ma yin kyang, nyan rang rnams rim gyis rgyud smin te 'tshang rgya ba'i thabs su 'gyur ba la 'gal ba ci yang med pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: And yet there is no such problem. Those two particular paths do represent going astray, from the path that people of greater capacity need to use to reach enlightenment with speed. As such, in this context we can say that they are not methods for becoming enlightened. But there is no contradiction at all in saying that these are methods for becoming enlightened from the point of view that they serve to ripen-in stages-the minds of the listeners and self-made buddhas.

rows.english: (12) The root downfall of causing a person to turn back from total enlightenment Committing this begins when you say the following to a person who has already developed the wish to achieve total enlightenment: You will never be able to carry out the six perfections, and actually reach Buddhahood.  If you strive instead for the goals of the listeners and self-made Buddhas, then you will manage to liberate yourself from the circle of suffering life." When because of your talking this way the person turns back from his or her wish to achieve full enlightenment, the downfall is complete.

rows.english: (14) The root downfall of holding that a person cannot eliminate desire and the rest by following the way of the learner You commit this when you hold that the realizations of listeners and self-made Buddhas could never liberate a person from the circle of suffering life: you discount the lesser way, saying "Regardless of how much a person might train himself in the ways of the listeners and the self-made Buddhas, he could never thereby eliminate the mental afflictions in their entirety."

rows.english: The first four lines [in the English] here summarize the meaning of the Wish for enlightenment, in both the form of a prayer, and action.  The next two lines summarize the five vows. The words "those who have yet to be freed" refer to beings such as the Pure One, Brahma, who are still bound in the fetters of ignorance and so on: the two kinds of obstacles; and we commit to free them. "Those who have yet to be saved" refers to those of the ways of listeners and self-made Buddhas, who are yet to be saved from the obstacles to omniscience; we commit to save them. "Those who have no comfort" is a reference to beings such as those in the realms of hell; we are resolving to bring them comfort.  And we decide finally to deliver all living beings to a state of nirvana which is beyond both of the extremes.  This is how both the Golden Harvest and the Explication of the Angel of Diamond both interpret these lines.  The Golden Harvest further explains the final verse as referring to the Wish for enlightenment in the form of action. ***

rows.acip: THEG PA DMAN PA NI CHED DU BYA BA GZHAN DON DANG 'BRAS BU BYANG CHUB DMAN PA NYAN RANG GI LAM STE, DE LA LAM DES RANG BGROD PAR 'DOD PA MI BYA BA YIN GYI THEG PA DMAN PA'I SDE SNOD KYIS BDAG LA CI BYA ZHES SPONG DU MI RUNG BAR SNGAR BSTAN ZIN TO,
rows.wylie: theg pa dman pa ni ched du bya ba gzhan don dang 'bras bu byang chub dman pa nyan rang gi lam ste, de la lam des rang bgrod par 'dod pa mi bya ba yin gyi theg pa dman pa'i sde snod kyis bdag la ci bya zhes spong du mi rung bar sngar bstan zin to
rows.english: What it means when we say that someone belongs to the "lesser" way is that the aim of their lives--the degree to which they work for others--and the goal they seek, the enlightenment they hope for, is a lower one. Thus they belong to the path of the listeners and self-made Buddhas. Here with this vow we are assuring that we feel no wish to use this path for our own spiritual journey; but still, as we've already mentioned before, it would be improper for us to reject this path, saying or thinking to ourselves: "What use would the group of teachings of the lesser way ever be for me"? *** Returning to Geshe Tsewang Samdrup:

rows.acip: GA-YON GYI 'DAB MAR 'JAM DBYANGS LA BYANG SEMS NYAN RANG DPA' BO MKHA 'GRO DANG BCAS PAS BSKOR BA, DE RNAMS KYI MTHA' SKOR DU BKA' SDOD KYI GTZO BO DUR BDAG DANG PHYAG BZHI PA SOGS CHOS SKYONG SRUNG MA DANG BCAS PA'I DGE 'DUN DKON MCHOG RNAMS GSAL LEGS PAR BTAB,
rows.wylie: ga-yon gyi 'dab mar 'jam dbyangs la byang sems nyan rang dpa' bo mkha 'gro dang bcas pas bskor ba, de rnams kyi mtha' skor du bka' sdod kyi gtso bo dur bdag dang phyag bzhi pa sogs chos skyong srung ma dang bcas pa'i dge 'dun dkon mchog rnams gsal legs par btab
rows.english: On the petal to my Lama's left is the Jewel of the Community, represented by Gentle Voice.  He is surrounded by bodhisattvas, listeners, self-made buddhas, and Warriors together with their Angels.  Around them on the outer circle are the primary Keepers of the Dharma--including the Lord of the Burial Ground and the Four-Armed One--along with all of the Dharma Protectors.  Try to make this picture very clear in your mind.

rows.acip: GA YAS KYI 'DAB MAR STON PA THUB PA'I DBANG PO LA LONGS SKU DANG MCHOG GI SPRUL SKU'I SANGS RGYAS RNAMS KYIS BSKOR BA, GA YON DU RJE BTZUN 'JAM DBYANGS LA THEG PA GSUM GYI DGE 'DUN BYANG SEMS NYAN RANG DPA' BO MKHA' 'GRO'I TSOGS KYIS BSKOR BA,

rows.english: On the petal to our Lama's own right is the Teacher, the Lord of Victors, surrounded by Buddhas in both bodies of enjoyment and the classical bodies of emanation.
